description: Add a PURE, deterministic backtest engine in @mlb/shared and relocate the pure predict() into @mlb/shared so both the engine and the frontend can import it with no backend/network/Bedrock dependency. This satisfies Issue #16 acceptance criteria (1) deterministic seed-only backtest with fixed values verified in tests, and (3) Bedrock not called (the engine lives in shared and imports only pure code + seed JSON; it structurally cannot reach Bedrock, DynamoDB, or the network). Module boundary decision: move the pure predict logic to shared/src/predict.ts and re-export it from backend/src/predict/model.ts so existing backend imports and tests are unchanged; predict's behavior stays byte-identical.
steps: Create shared/src/predict.ts containing the EXACT current pure prediction logic moved verbatim from backend/src/predict/model.ts: export `predict`, `PredictionResult`, `WinPctMap`, and `teamName`, importing MIN_ACCURACY/MAX_ACCURACY/DEFAULT_ACCURACY/TEAMS/Bracket/Series from the sibling shared modules (use relative './accuracy.js', './types.js'). Keep the clamp bounds (MIN_PROB=0.5, MAX_PROB=0.95), the sharpening factor f=2*accuracy around floor 0.5, the 4-decimal rounding, and all JSDoc. Do NOT change any numeric behavior.

Update backend/src/predict/model.ts to RE-EXPORT from @mlb/shared instead of defining the logic: `export { predict, teamName, MIN_ACCURACY, MAX_ACCURACY, DEFAULT_ACCURACY } from '@mlb/shared'; export type { PredictionResult, WinPctMap } from '@mlb/shared';`. This preserves every existing backend import path (backend/src/index.ts, service/bracketService.ts, bedrock/narrative.ts, store/dynamo.ts, predict/standings.ts) and keeps backend/src/predict/model.test.ts and model.property.test.ts green unchanged.

Add predict + the new names to the @mlb/shared barrel: in shared/src/index.ts add `export * from './predict.js';` (ensure no duplicate export conflicts with accuracy re-exports; predict.ts should NOT re-export the accuracy constants to avoid barrel collisions — import them internally only).

Create shared/src/backtest.ts implementing the pure engine. Define and document the semantics precisely in JSDoc: (a) 'predict at the end of game k' means: for a given final series, for each k in 1..series.games.length, build a PARTIAL Series whose `games` is the first k games (sorted by seriesGameNumber ascending) and whose high.wins/low.wins are RECOMPUTED by counting winners among those first k games (do not trust the series' final wins); status set to 'in_progress' when k < games.length else 'final'; then call predict(partialSeries, bracket, {}, accuracy). (b) The outcome label is the EVENTUAL SERIES WINNER = the team id with the greater final win total (high vs low) in the full series; ties cannot occur in a decided best-of series. Only include series with status 'final' and at least one game.

In backtest.ts define types: `BacktestSample { seriesId, round, gameNumber, favoriteTeamId, favoriteWinProbability, eventualWinnerTeamId, favoriteWasCorrect, probOfEventualWinner }` where probOfEventualWinner = favoriteWinProbability if favoriteTeamId === eventualWinnerTeamId else 1 - favoriteWinProbability. `CalibrationBin { lowerInclusive, upperExclusive (last bin upper inclusive), predictedCount, meanPredictedProbability, empiricalWinRate }`. `BacktestResult { accuracy, sampleCount, hitRate, brierScore, calibrationBins }`. `MultiSeasonBacktest { accuracy, seasons: number[], perSeason: Record<number, BacktestResult>, combined: BacktestResult }`.

Implement `runBacktest(bracket: Bracket, accuracy: number): BacktestResult`: iterate final series, produce samples per the semantics above. hitRate = mean(favoriteWasCorrect ? 1 : 0). brierScore = mean( (probOfEventualWinner - 1)^2 ) — i.e. squared error of the probability assigned to the team that actually won the series. Round hitRate and brierScore to a fixed precision (e.g. 6 decimals) using a documented helper so expected test values are stable. Calibration: fixed bins over the FAVORITE probability [0.5,0.95]; use 5 equal-width buckets edges [0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95] (document that the model's output range is [0.5,0.95]); for each bucket compute predictedCount, meanPredictedProbability (mean favoriteWinProbability of samples in bucket), and empiricalWinRate (fraction of those samples where the favorite was correct). Empty buckets report count 0 and null/0 for means (choose one and document; prefer meanPredictedProbability=null, empiricalWinRate=null when count=0).

Implement `runMultiSeasonBacktest(accuracy: number, seasons?: number[]): MultiSeasonBacktest` defaulting seasons to [2024, 2025], importing POSTSEASON_2024/POSTSEASON_2025 from the seed barrel; perSeason runs runBacktest per bracket; combined aggregates across ALL samples of all seasons (recompute hitRate/brier/calibration over the pooled samples, not by averaging per-season metrics). Also export a small helper `runBacktestAcrossAccuracies(accuracies: number[], seasons?: number[]): { accuracy, combined, perSeason }[]` to support the slider comparison (default accuracies [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]).

Write shared/src/backtest.test.ts (Vitest) with FIXED expected numbers (criterion 1). First compute the real numbers by running the engine once during development, then PIN them as literals: assert exact hitRate and brierScore for runBacktest(POSTSEASON_2024, 0.5), runBacktest(POSTSEASON_2025, 0.5), and runMultiSeasonBacktest(0.5).combined. Also assert sampleCount equals the total number of games across all final series for that season (2024: sum of games per final series; 2025 likewise). Assert accuracy=0 collapses every favoriteWinProbability to 0.5 so brierScore == 0.25 exactly and probOfEventualWinner == 0.5 for all samples. Assert calibration bins: predictedCount across bins sums to sampleCount; at accuracy=0 all samples fall in the [0.5,0.6) bucket. Assert monotonic/behavioral edge: an empty bracket (no final series) yields sampleCount 0 and hitRate/brier handled without NaN (define and document the empty-case return, e.g. hitRate=0, brierScore=0, empty bins).

Write shared/src/backtest.property.test.ts (fast-check): for random accuracy in [0,1] over the real 2024/2025 brackets, assert hitRate in [0,1], brierScore in [0,1], every calibrationBin.empiricalWinRate (when count>0) in [0,1], and sum of bin counts === sampleCount. Keep iterations modest for speed.
Run the shared unit + property tests and the FULL `npm test` to confirm backend predict tests still pass unchanged.

After the engine is implemented and the real numbers are known, update this feature's findings with the concrete pinned values (2024 hitRate/brier, 2025 hitRate/brier, combined at accuracy 0.5, and sampleCounts) so FEAT-003's UI/docs can quote them.
acceptance_criteria: shared/src/predict.ts holds the pure predict logic; backend/src/predict/model.ts re-exports it; all existing backend predict tests (model.test.ts, model.property.test.ts) pass unchanged

shared/src/backtest.ts exports runBacktest, runMultiSeasonBacktest, runBacktestAcrossAccuracies and the result types, importing only pure shared code + seed JSON (no AWS/Bedrock/network/DynamoDB imports)

shared/src/backtest.test.ts asserts FIXED literal hitRate and brierScore for 2024, 2025, and the combined run at accuracy 0.5, plus the accuracy=0 => brierScore 0.25 invariant and calibration-count invariants
shared/src/backtest.property.test.ts asserts hitRate and brierScore are within [0,1] across random accuracy values
`npm run build` and `npm test` both pass
findings: Implemented on branch feat/mlb-postseason-site; source commit 6800d91. Moved the pure predict() logic verbatim into shared/src/predict.ts (exports predict, PredictionResult, WinPctMap, teamName; imports MIN/MAX/DEFAULT_ACCURACY internally from './accuracy.js' and does NOT re-export them to avoid a barrel collision with './accuracy.js'). backend/src/predict/model.ts is now a thin re-export from @mlb/shared (predict, teamName, MIN/MAX/DEFAULT_ACCURACY + PredictionResult/WinPctMap types); all existing backend predict tests pass UNCHANGED (model.test.ts 12 tests, model.property.test.ts 6 tests; 0.8093 regression guard still green). Added shared/src/backtest.ts (runBacktest, runMultiSeasonBacktest, runBacktestAcrossAccuracies + types BacktestSample/CalibrationBin/BacktestResult/MultiSeasonBacktest/AccuracyBacktest), importing only ./predict.js, ./types.js, ./seed/index.js (no AWS/Bedrock/DynamoDB/network). Barrel shared/src/index.ts now has `export * from './predict.js';` and `export * from './backtest.js';`. Metrics rounded to 6 decimals via roundMetric. Empty-case contract: sampleCount 0 => hitRate 0, brierScore 0, empty bins (no NaN). PINNED VALUES at accuracy 0.5: 2024 hitRate=0.906977 brierScore=0.134132 sampleCount=43; 2025 hitRate=0.744681 brierScore=0.194365 sampleCount=47; combined (pooled 2024+2025) hitRate=0.822222 brierScore=0.165587 sampleCount=90. Invariants verified: accuracy=0 => brierScore===0.25 exactly and all samples land in the [0.5,0.6) bucket (count===sampleCount, meanPredictedProbability===0.5); calibration bin counts sum to sampleCount across accuracies 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1; empty bins report null means. Property test (fast-check, 100 runs over real 2024/2025 brackets, random accuracy): hitRate & brierScore in [0,1], populated-bin empiricalWinRate in [0,1], bin counts sum to sampleCount. Verification: `npm run build -w @mlb/shared`, `npm test -w @mlb/shared` (34 tests, 6 files), full `npm run build`, and full `npm test` all exit 0 (backend 92 tests green, infra 8 green with pre-existing harmless nodejs20.x W2531 deprecation warnings). These pinned numbers are available for FEAT-003's UI/docs to quote. Did NOT push or open a PR.
